scenario: A clinical outcomes registry includes only patients who survive one year and whose quality-of-life score exceeds 70. A health-system administrator uses the registry's mean score to estimate the typical one-year quality of care across all treated patients.

data.description: Only survivors with quality-of-life score > 70 enter the registry. Scores are modeled as Normal with known standard deviation sigma = 15.

question: Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean one-year quality-of-life score mu across all treated patients and (b) the fraction of treated patients that appear in the registry.
naive_answer: Typical one-year quality of care is about 76.8 because that is the registry mean.
naive_trap: The registry excludes both non-survivors and low-scoring survivors, so it contains only a selected upper tail of outcomes.
reasoning_trace: Step 1: Solve 76.81 = mu + 15*lambda((70-mu)/15). Step 2: The solution has alpha about 1.4, so mu = 70 - 1.4*15 = 49. Step 3: The registry fraction is sf(1.4) about 0.0808.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu):
    a=(70-mu)/15
    return mu + 15*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a) - 76.81
mu=brentq(eq,-100,69.99)
frac=norm.sf((70-mu)/15)
assert abs(mu-49.0)<0.8 and abs(frac-0.0808)<0.005
